plan.contextChunk: This figure is a dimensioned elevation drawing of a natural draft cooling tower, rendered as a translucent orange solid of revolution. The silhouette is widest at ground level, sweeps inward to a narrow waist above the midpoint, then flares slightly outward again to a flat circular top. The left half of the shell carries many closely spaced vertical contour lines following the curvature, while the right half is left as a smooth tinted surface, and a row of small teal angled supports rings the open base. A vertical dashed line runs up the center as the axis, and a horizontal dashed line crosses it at the waist. Four measurements are marked with double-headed arrows: 72 m across the top rim, 60 m across the narrow waist, 79.6 m from the top down to the waist level, and 179.6 m for the full height from ground to top, drawn along a long dimension line at the far left. Placing both diameters and both heights against the same profile makes the whole shape recoverable from four numbers. The layout supplies the data for fitting a hyperbola, centered where the dashed lines intersect, to the curved sides of the tower.

elements: translucent pale orange 3D hyperboloid shell
vertical curved contour lines along the left half of the 3D surface
ring of small teal angled column supports around the base
left and right solid orange 2D hyperbolic profile curves
vertical dashed center axis line
horizontal dashed line at the waist level (y = 100 m)
horizontal dimension line and label '72 m' across the top rim
horizontal dimension line and label '60 m' across the narrow waist
vertical dimension line and label '79.6 m' from waist to top
full-height vertical dimension line and label '179.6 m' at the far left
dynamic horizontal measurement line crossing the entire width at current height
dynamic text label indicating the calculated diameter at the current height

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching between 2D and 3D clarifies how the flat hyperbolic profile and its dimensions define the full solid of revolution.

interactions.label: Height (m)
interactions.teaches: Moving the height line reveals how the diameter expands hyperbolically from the narrow waist towards the top and base.
Rotating the 3D model shows the circular cross-sections and rotational symmetry of the hyperboloid.

demo_steps.title: The Hyperbolic Profile
demo_steps.narration: The tower's shape is defined by a hyperbola. The narrowest point (waist) is 60 m across, and the top is 72 m across, sitting 79.6 m above the waist.

demo_steps.title: Expanding Diameter
demo_steps.narration: Move the height slider up and down. The diameter grows non-linearly away from the waist, reaching roughly 78.1 m at the ground level.

demo_steps.title: Solid of Revolution
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the 3D view shows how this 2D hyperbola is swept around the vertical axis to form the shell of the cooling tower.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Scale: 1 world unit = 10 meters. Origin at center of the base (ground level). Total height = 17.96 units. Waist is at y = 10.0 units. Top is at y = 17.96 units. The cross-sectional radius r(y) = 3.0 * sqrt(1 + (y - 10.0)^2 / 144.0036). Colors: Tower shell is pale orange #fad2bc, contour lines are #e39a78, base supports are teal #7ab0b3, dimension lines and text are black. For the 3D shell, use a lathe geometry with opacity 0.6. Base supports can be modeled as small tilted cylinders from y=0 to y=0.5, angled outwards to match the shell base radius (r=3.905). The dynamic measurement line spans from -r(y) to +r(y) at the slider's y position, with its text updating to the diameter (20 * r(y)) formatted to 1 decimal place.
interactionPlan.notes: Reactively update the position of the dynamic measurement line and its label text whenever the height slider changes. When the viewMode toggle is '2D Profile', hide the 3D shell, contour lines, and 3D base supports, and optionally tween the camera back to azimuth 90 to match the elevation drawing. In '3D Tower' mode, reveal the 3D elements.

authoredContext:
The design layout of a cooling tower is shown in the figure. The tower stands 179.6 meters tall. The diameter of the top is 72 meters. At their closest, the sides of the tower are 60 meters apart.

Project design for a natural draft cooling tower

A diagram illustrating the dimensions of a hyperbolic cooling tower, showing a total height of 179.6 m, an upper section height of 79.6 m, an upper diameter of 72 m, and a narrower waist diameter of 60 m.

Find the equation of the hyperbola that models the sides of the cooling tower. Assume that the center of the hyperbola—indicated by the intersection of dashed perpendicular lines in the figure—is the origin of the coordinate plane. Round final values to four decimal places.

discrepancies: The 2D view is an empty wireframe outline, missing the pale orange fill and the curved contour lines on the left half.
All dimension text labels are completely absent from the visual output.
The base supports are rendered as a thin zig-zag wireframe instead of solid teal blocks and V-shapes.
The vertical dimension lines are placed too far left with overlapping extensions, rather than nested closely to the tower.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure includes good interactive features, but completely fails to replicate the visual style of the 2D source diagram, presenting an empty wireframe without labels instead of a filled, styled shape.
action_items: Render the 2D tower using a filled THREE.ShapeGeometry with a pale orange color instead of an empty wireframe.
Add the curved vertical contour lines to the left half of the 2D profile to match the source figure.
Draw the base supports using solid teal shapes rather than a thin zig-zag line.
Fix label rendering to ensure all dimension text is visible and correctly positioned.

discrepancies: Base supports are rendered as a simple continuous zig-zag, whereas the original has vertical rectangular pillars with diagonal struts
The original has a distinct horizontal line and vertical edge at the bottom right of the tower shell, which are missing in the generated figure
The vertical contour lines on the left half of the tower are faintly rendered compared to the distinct lines in the source
The dynamic blue measurement line directly overlaps and obscures the static 60m waist measurement when positioned at the waist
evaluation.notes: Excellent interactive figure that correctly models the hyperbola and its measurements, though it misses some specific architectural details at the base.
action_items: Redraw the bottom base supports to include vertical rectangular pillars with diagonal struts rather than a simple V-shaped zig-zag
Add the missing horizontal line and vertical edge detail to the bottom right half of the 2D tower profile
Increase the linewidth or adjust the color of the left-side contour lines to make them more distinct
Offset the dynamic blue measurement line vertically by a small amount so it does not obscure the static 60m dashed waistline when at y=10

feedback.rationale: Scores are consistently high (4s and 5s, overall 4.4) with no failure modes, indicating the figure is excellent and only has minor aesthetic discrepancies that do not detract from the core concept.
